newsitem.title: GERMANY: Tietmeyer hopes for EMU progress on stability pact.
newsitem.headline: Tietmeyer hopes for EMU progress on stability pact.

text.p: Bundesbank President Hans Tietmeyer said on Tuesday he was hopeful for progress toward a stability pact to be implemented after currency union at upcoming European Union meetings in Dublin.
"We have agreed that a stability pact is necessary and that it must be an efficient one," Tietmeyer told Reuters Financial Television in an interview.
"I am very hopeful that we can come to a result," he said.
European finance and economics ministers are scheduled to meet this weekend in Dublin for an informal session and then return to Dublin in December for a formal meeting.
No official decisions are reached at the informal meetings but the groundwork for the later meeting are made.
Tietmeyer also said he was very hopeful for an agreement at the Dublin meetings on "ins" and "pre-ins".
When asked whether a decision will be taken on the relationship between countries who will participate in the launch of the single currency and those outside, he said:
"I hope so, because on the agenda of the Dublin meeting will be on one hand the stability pact and also the so-called pre-ins and outs relationship."
